title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android: call quality feedback surveys after meetings
summary: Hold: Microsoft now identifies the Android app update introducing these surveys and explicitly links their control to feedback policies, so the briefing's corresponding documentation gaps are out of date. It also presents the Message Center post's end date as a rollout end date that the notice does not give.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy route is Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. On the Start with the basics page, enter a name ... On the Choose the scope page ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies
claims.fix: The printed route correctly reaches the settings page but stops before its named control. Append ' > Allow users to receive and respond to in-product surveys from Microsoft' to controls[0].ui.path; feedback-manage documents searching for 'feedback' or 'survey' there and gives this policy name.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no configuration PowerShell, Graph or other API for this Cloud Policy survey setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cloud Policy" PowerShell Graph API create policy configuration; "Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365" "API"; "Cloud Policy" "PowerShell" "survey". Opened overview-cloud-policy and feedback-manage; found no configuration call, only audit API references.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy is a documented way to disable Teams Rooms in-product surveys including call quality feedback prompts.
claims.quote: Teams Rooms devices may display in-product surveys, including call quality feedback prompts, to signed-in room accounts. To disable these surveys, use the Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.
